title: The Geometry of Hindustani Music
subtitle: Continuous Manifolds, Thermodynamic Time Theory, and the Generative Grammar of Raga

blocks.text: This chapter presents the poster “The Geometry of Hindustani Music” in full. It is a single dense diagram; open it, then use the explanation, read-aloud, and Ask-AI tools beneath it to work through the ideas at your own pace.

blocks.caption: Figure 9.1 — The Geometry of Hindustani Music.
blocks.explanation: Hindustani music is modelled as a continuous manifold, in contrast to the discrete combinatorial lattice of the Carnatic Melakarta system. The ten Thaats are base coordinate frames; a Raga is a directed geodesic and potential well defined by ascent/descent directionality, a signature Pakad motif, and Nyas gravitational attractors; Shruti and Meend are continuous-manifold traversal through twenty-two microtones. A thermodynamic time-theory couples ragas to the circadian rhythm, and a formal generative grammar produces valid improvisation as a parse tree. Raga is presented not as a scale but as a living geometry of sound, time, and consciousness.
blocks.tts: Hindustani music as continuous geometry: thaats as coordinate frames, ragas as directed geodesics through microtonal space, coupled to the daily cycle by a thermodynamic time-theory.
